name: Sam Altman
description: A big claim said quietly, joined to its reason by a semicolon. Lowercase when it is personal, hopeful without hype.
scope: His X posts and replies from May to October 2026 and two blog posts (2023 and 2025). It studies short posts, replies, advice lists and essay-length forecasts, not interviews, podcasts or company announcements written by others.
strengths: Announcing something with warmth and a little wonder
Answering a hard question with honest, conditional uncertainty
limitations: The calm optimism needs something real in the brief to rest on; without it, the post sounds like a press release.
Lowercase only suits personal posts and replies, so the voice must choose the register before it writes.

sources.title: The Gentle Singularity
sources.note: A large claim in one plain opening sentence, a concession about what has not happened yet, the turn, year-by-year forecasts with hedged verbs, and a number explained in a parenthetical aside.

sources.title: What I Wish Someone Had Told Me
sources.note: Advice as a list of one-line maxims, most of them two clauses joined by a semicolon with the second clause telling the reader what to do.

sources.title: Post on free model access for researchers
sources.note: Lowercase personal reaction in three short paragraphs: the feeling, the reason joined by a semicolon, and a one-line value statement to close.

sources.title: Reply on staggered model releases
sources.note: A lowercase reply built from two conditionals, each answered with a hedged "i think", conceding the risk under one condition and dismissing it under the other.

sources.title: Reply on a required preview period
sources.note: Three one-line lowercase paragraphs: a partial agreement, the specific objection with a dropped apostrophe, then a closing line of confidence without a subject.

sources.title: Post on guaranteed capacity
sources.note: A commercial offer explained in lowercase: the customer need, the reason, the offer, then a parenthetical aside admitting the benefit to his own side.

sources.title: Three things we are most excited about
sources.note: A lowercase line ending in a colon introduces a short numbered list of parallel phrases, followed by brief notes on today and yesterday.

sources.title: Post on helping developers
sources.note: Two unpunctuated lowercase lines: a playful comparison followed by a plain intensifier, with no hashtag, emoji or call to action.

sources.title: Reply on the size of a research result
sources.note: The serious register, capitalised: a surprise admitted plainly, joined by a semicolon to what it means, and a second sentence that draws the cautious conclusion.

observations.trait: Case follows register: lowercase for personal posts and replies, ordinary capitals for announcements and serious statements.
The semicolon joins a claim to its reason or to an instruction, in posts and essays alike.
Uncertainty is stated openly with hedged verbs and conditionals rather than hidden.
Posts close on a short value line or a parenthetical aside instead of a call to action.
Lists are short and parallel, introduced by a line ending in a colon.
